subject: Urgent: real-time ingestion throttling causing spikes in latency and 429s — exec attention needed
messages:
From: Mitchell Hayes <mitch.hayes@acme-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: High latency + 429s hitting ingestion pipeline (real-time)

Hannah —

We're seeing a major degradation on our real-time ingestion pipeline into Redwood since ~07:50 PT. Token-level latency for our streaming requests has gone from ~60ms p50 to 900ms p95 and we're getting intermittent 429s. Throughput is also dropping; our dashboard shows sustained 30% reduction in accepted requests. This is impacting live features for several customers.

Quick artifacts attached: screenshot_429.png, redwood_request_id_7891.log (sample 429/latency traces).

Can you confirm if this is a known rollout or config change on your side? We need an ETA — this is on-call for our SLOs.

—Mitchell

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + 429s hitting ingestion pipeline (real-time)

Short initial findings (prelim):

- Root symptom: rapid token-burst from a scheduled backfill job at 07:47 PT caused the customer's dedicated pool's token bucket to exhaust. Because the customer's quota config combined a conservative per-second rate limit with a tight burst window, we rapidly started returning 429 while the autoscaler and fallback policies couldn't react in time.
- Error pattern: 429s from the serving layer (rate limiter), followed by queueing at proxies causing p95 latency to spike. Not a model compute regression.
- Evidence: attached burst_policy_config.yaml snippet and sampled request IDs indicate token-bucket depletion.

Mitigation in-flight:
1) Temporarily increase burst window + rate cap for account ACME-67890 for 4 hours (we can do this from the control plane).
2) Enable automatic fallback to the compatible smaller model variant for requests that hit the burst threshold (reduces tokens per request).
3) Apply a short-lived traffic-shaping rule to smooth the backfill (we've asked Acme to throttle the backfill job).

I believe this is a misconfiguration rather than an infra outage. I'll follow up with a diff of the config and propose a durable quota/burst correction.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
